last-stone-weight.d: Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones: equal stones vanish, otherwise the difference remains. Return the last stone's weight (or 0).
last-stone-weight.i: Max-heap: poll two, push the difference if it's non-zero.

letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.d: Given digits 2-9, return all letter strings they could represent on a phone keypad.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.i: Backtracking: at index i, loop over the letters of digits[i], append one, recurse to i+1, then remove it.

linked-list-cycle.d: Determine whether a linked list contains a cycle.
linked-list-cycle.ex: 3->2->0->-4 with tail pointing to node 2 -> true
linked-list-cycle.i: Floyd: slow moves 1, fast moves 2; if there's a cycle they meet, otherwise fast reaches null. A HashSet of visited nodes also works with O(n) space.

linked-list-cycle-ii.d: Return the node where a linked list's cycle begins, or null if there is no cycle.
linked-list-cycle-ii.ex: 3->2->0->-4 with tail pointing to node 2 -> node 2
linked-list-cycle-ii.i: After slow and fast meet, reset slow to head and move both one step at a time; they meet at the cycle start. (The distance from head to the start equals the distance from the meeting point to the start, modulo the cycle length.)
k: Floyd meet, then reset to head

longest-common-prefix.d: Return the longest common prefix shared by all strings in the array.
longest-common-prefix.i: Vertical scan: compare character i across all strings up to the shortest length. Trick: after sorting, only the first and last strings need comparing.
k: Vertical scan up to min length

longest-common-subsequence.d: Return the length of the longest common subsequence of two strings.
longest-common-subsequence.i: f(i, j) = 1 + f(i-1, j-1) if chars match, else max(f(i-1, j), f(i, j-1)). The base pattern for many string DPs (edit distance, delete operations, palindromic subsequence).

longest-consecutive-sequence.d: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers present in an unsorted array, in O(n).
longest-consecutive-sequence.i: Put everything in a HashSet. Only start counting from numbers with no predecessor (x-1 not in set) and walk upward, so each number is visited O(1) times.
k: HashSet, count only from sequence starts

longest-increasing-subsequence.d: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
longest-increasing-subsequence.i: DP over (index, previous index): take nums[i] if it's larger than the previous, or skip it. O(n log n) alternative: keep a 'tails' array and binary-search where each number goes.

longest-palindromic-subsequence.d: Return the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of s.
longest-palindromic-subsequence.i: A palindromic subsequence reads the same reversed, so the answer = LCS(s, reverse(s)).
k: LCS of s and its reverse

longest-palindromic-substring.d: Return the longest palindromic substring of s.
longest-palindromic-substring.i: Expand around each centre: 2n-1 centres (each character and each gap). Expand while the ends match and keep the longest.

longest-repeating-character-replacement.d: You may change at most k characters. Return the longest substring that can be made of one repeated letter.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.i: Sliding window: it's valid while windowLen - maxFreq <= k. Grow the right edge; if invalid, move left once. maxFreq never needs to decrease, because only a larger maxFreq can give a longer answer.
k: Sliding window, recompute max over 26 counts

longest-substring-without-repeating-char.d: Return the length of the longest substring with all distinct characters.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.i: Sliding window with a set: extend right; on a repeat, shrink from the left until it's gone. Faster: store each char's last index and jump left = max(left, last[c] + 1).
k: Window with HashSet (shrink one by one)

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.d: Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary search tree.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.i: Use the BST order: if both values are smaller go left, if both are larger go right; otherwise the current node is where they split, so it's the LCA.
k: Follow BST order until p and q split

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.d: Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a general binary tree.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.i: Return the node if it's null, p or q. Recurse left and right: if both sides return non-null, this node is the LCA; otherwise pass up the non-null side.

lru-cache.d: Design a Least-Recently-Used cache with O(1) get and put that evicts the least recently used key when full.
lru-cache.ex: cap 2: put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1)=1, put(3,3) evicts 2, get(2)=-1
lru-cache.i: HashMap key -> node plus a doubly linked list ordered by recency, with dummy head and tail. On access, move the node to the front; on overflow, remove the node before the tail.

majority-element.d: Return the element that appears more than n/2 times (it always exists).
majority-element.i: Boyer-Moore voting: keep a candidate and a count. Matching elements increment, others decrement, and at count 0 take a new candidate. The majority survives.

majority-element-ii.d: Return all elements appearing more than n/3 times.
majority-element-ii.i: At most two such elements exist. Extended Boyer-Moore with two candidates and two counts, then a second pass to verify each candidate's count.

max-area-of-island.d: Return the area of the largest 4-directionally connected island of 1s in a grid.
max-area-of-island.i: Flood-fill each unvisited land cell (DFS or BFS) and count the cells reached; keep the maximum.

max-consecutive-ones.d: Return the longest run of consecutive 1s in a binary array.
max-consecutive-ones.i: Running counter that resets on 0; track the maximum.

maximum-average-pass-ratio.d: Each class has pass/total students. Add extraStudents guaranteed passers to classes to maximise the average pass ratio.
maximum-average-pass-ratio.i: Greedy with a max-heap ordered by the gain (p+1)/(t+1) - p/t. Always give the next student to the class with the biggest gain, then push it back with its new gain.
